reasons: Deviation classification is sound: the only ownership provision (p0029) unilaterally confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface and the document contains no Customer Data/IP retention statement and no assignment or perpetual licence-back for Support Services deliverables, so the clause fails the fallback (which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables), not merely the preferred position.

The redline is directionally correct and targeted: it leaves TrueLink's Interface ownership intact, adds Client retention of Client Content/IP/borrower data, a no-assignment/no-joint-ownership statement, and an assignment of Support Services work product with a carve-out plus embedded-IP licence back — exactly the operations in the redline guidance.

Interaction with the existing broad Credit Data licence (p0054) is handled correctly by expressly preserving it rather than reopening it, avoiding an internally inconsistent edit and double-flagging of a negotiated carve-out.

The failed 'minimal edit' check is advisory only here: the changed-character ratio reflects added sentences on top of the retained original text, which is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position for a clause that is silent on Customer Data and deliverables.

Comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, states what changed, cites the playbook position, and correctly notes that TrueLink's Interface ownership and Section 8(d) are untouched; the only nit is reliance on the inferred 'Section 8(d)' cross-reference, which should be confirmed against final numbering.
